name: Meetings
title: AI prompts for meeting notes and action items
description: Copy-paste prompts to turn meeting transcripts and notes into summaries, decisions and action items with owners and dates — without the AI inventing either.
intro: Meeting summaries fail in two ways: action items without an owner, and owners or dates the AI made up. These templates only record what was actually said and flag everything that is missing.

templates.title: Notes to action items
templates.useWhen: Right after any meeting with tasks.
templates.prompt:
From the meeting notes between <<< and >>>, extract a table: action | owner | due date | source quote.
Rules: only include actions someone actually agreed to; if an owner or date wasn't stated, write “not assigned” or “no date” — never guess; the source quote is the line in the notes that supports the action.

Notes: <<<[PASTE]>>>
templates.why: The source quote makes every item checkable, and “not assigned” turns a missing owner into a follow-up instead of a fiction.

templates.title: Decisions and open questions
templates.useWhen: A long discussion where nobody is sure what was decided.
templates.prompt:
From this transcript, list: 1) decisions made (and who made them), 2) questions raised but not resolved, 3) disagreements that were left open. Only what was said — don't infer decisions from discussion.

Transcript: <<<[PASTE]>>>
templates.why: Discussion is not a decision. Three separate lists show what is actually settled.

templates.title: Recap email to attendees
templates.useWhen: Everyone needs the same version of what happened.
templates.prompt:
Write a recap email from these notes: <<<[PASTE]>>>
Structure: one sentence on the purpose of the meeting; decisions as bullets; action items with owner and date (write “TBC” where missing); the next meeting if mentioned. Under 200 words. Ask attendees to reply with corrections by [DATE].
templates.why: Asking for corrections turns the recap into the source of truth — and catches the AI's mistakes early.

templates.title: An agenda that ends on time
templates.prompt:
Create an agenda for a [MINUTES]-minute meeting with [ATTENDEES OR ROLES]. Goal: by the end we will have decided [DECISION].
For each item: the question it answers, the owner, the minutes and any pre-reading. Put the decision item first. If the goal doesn't fit the time, tell me what to cut.
templates.why: Agenda items phrased as questions end in answers, and putting the decision first protects it from running out of time.

templates.title: Brief someone who missed the meeting
templates.useWhen: A colleague was absent and needs only what affects them.
templates.prompt:
[NAME] missed this meeting. From the notes below, write a 5-bullet brief of what matters for their role ([ROLE]): decisions that affect them, actions assigned to them and anything they need to respond to. Nothing else.

Notes: <<<[PASTE]>>>
templates.why: A role-specific brief is far more useful than a generic summary, and the filter keeps it short.

templates.title: Clean up a raw transcript
templates.useWhen: An automatic transcript is full of errors and filler.
templates.prompt:
Clean up this automatic transcript: fix obvious speech-to-text errors, remove filler words, and split it into paragraphs by topic with short headings. Don't summarise, reword opinions or remove content. Mark words you couldn't make sense of as [unclear].

Transcript: <<<[PASTE]>>>
templates.why: Cleaning is not summarising. Keeping the content intact and marking [unclear] preserves a faithful record.
